about: Synthetic content for the 24-call Jev probe. Every turn, statement and project detail is invented; none comes from a real prompt, person or stored judgment.

states.short: Please update the ferry timetable importer so it skips rows with a blank departure time, and add a test for that case. The importer lives in the schedule module. Keep the change small: we ship the weekend timetable on Friday and I do not want to touch the fare rules this week. If a row has a blank arrival time but a valid departure, keep it and log a warning instead of dropping it.
long: We are working on the harbor ferry ticketing app, a small web service that sells tickets for four island routes and prints boarding passes at the dock kiosks. The code is a Python service with a SQLite database, a nightly timetable import, and a small admin page that the dock staff use to correct sailings when the weather changes. Tests run on every push, and a release goes out most Fridays after the weekend timetable is checked.

Today's task is the timetable importer. The operators send a spreadsheet export every week, and the last two exports had rows with a blank departure time where a sailing was cancelled but not removed. The importer currently treats a blank as midnight, so the kiosk showed phantom sailings at 00:00 and two passengers bought tickets for boats that never left. The fix should skip a row with no departure time and say so in the import log.

A row with a valid departure but a blank arrival is different. Arrival times are often missing for the short hop to the north island, because the crossing takes eight minutes and the operator never fills it in. Those rows must stay. The importer should keep them, fill nothing in, and write a warning line with the route code and the row number so the admin page can show which sailings lack an arrival.

There is a second, older problem in the same module that we are not fixing today. Fares are looked up by route and by season, and the season boundaries are hard-coded for last year. Someone will need to move them into the database, but that touches the fare rules, the receipts and the refund screen, and it is too big to do before Friday. Please leave the fare code exactly as it is, even if a test there looks wrong.

The test suite has a fixtures folder with three sample exports. Add a fourth that has one blank departure, one blank arrival and one normal row, and write tests that check the importer keeps two rows, skips one, and logs one warning. The existing tests use plain asserts and a temporary database per test, and they should keep doing that. Do not add a new test framework or a new dependency for this change.

Last time the assistant changed the importer it also reformatted the whole module, which made the review hard to read and hid a real change to the date parsing. This time keep the diff to the lines that need to change. If something else in the module looks broken, write it down in the summary at the end instead of fixing it in the same change, and say how sure you are that it is broken.

The kiosk team asked whether the importer could also reject sailings that leave before the previous one on the same route, since that usually means the operator typed a time in the wrong column. That is a good idea but it needs their sign-off on what to do with the rejected rows, so it is out of scope here. Mention it in the summary as a follow-up and do not build it yet.

For the import log, use the same format as the existing lines: a timestamp, the level, the route code, the row number and a short reason. Keep reasons to a few fixed words such as blank_departure or blank_arrival so the admin page can count them. Do not log passenger names or ticket numbers; the timetable export never has them, and the log must stay free of anything personal if that ever changes.

When you are done, run the whole test suite, not only the importer tests, because the kiosk rendering tests read the imported timetable and can break in ways that are hard to spot. If any test fails that you did not touch, stop and report it rather than changing the test. The release checklist says a red suite blocks the Friday release, and nobody wants to explain a missed weekend timetable to the island operators.

Finally, write a short summary: what changed, which tests were added, what you ran, what you noticed but did not fix, and anything you are unsure about. Keep it plain and short so the dock lead can read it on a phone between sailings. If you had to guess about anything in the export format, say which guess you made and how to check it against next week's spreadsheet before the release goes out.

templates: Always back up {x} before changing it
Run the full test suite after touching {x}
Keep changes to {x} as small as the task allows
Write down in the summary anything odd about {x} instead of fixing it silently
Do not add a new dependency for work on {x}
Explain in plain words why {x} changed
Check {x} on a phone-sized screen before calling it done
Prefer fixed reason codes over free text when logging about {x}
Leave {x} alone when the task does not name it
Say how sure you are before claiming {x} is broken
Keep the old behaviour of {x} unless the task says otherwise
Stop and report a failing test in {x} rather than editing the test
